text:
jen: Holding the release cut — canary failed on integration tests, deploy-bot aborted promote.

deploy-bot: [automated] promote aborted: canary check failed (service-e2e: timeout). see job 4821. retry disabled for change-window.

ryan: I looked at the canary logs. The failing test is `payment::refund_flow` timing out repeatedly at the external-payments mock handshake.

boa: That mock started timing out after the dependency bump to paymock v2.1.0 in the canary image. v2.0.7 worked fine.

jen: Change window closes in 90m. Options:
- pin service image to last-good sha and promote manually
- revert dependency bump in the build and re-run canary
- abort cut and roll to next window

release-coordinator: Manual pin is fastest but loses automation. Revert+rebuild may take ~30-45m if ci queue cooperates. Thoughts?

ryan: Revert looks better for traceability. I can open a quick revert PR to CI: `ci/reverts/revert-paymock-2.1.0` and trigger a canary rebuild. If tests pass we keep automated promote.

boa: If CI is congested and rebuild stalls, fallback to pinning to sha:0123deadbeef and we do a manual promote. I'll prepare the pinned image just in case.

jen: Ok do revert first. @ryan please kick the PR and mark it high priority. @boa hold the pin ready.

ryan: PR opened: https://git/repo/PR/2748 — branch revert-paymock-2.1.0. Triggering pipeline now.

deploy-bot: canary pipeline triggered by @ryan. polling for status...

ryan: Pipeline passed canary e2e on first attempt! All checks green.

deploy-bot: promote triggered by @ryan. attempting promote... promote succeeded: release-2026-03-23 -> production. :tada:

jen: Nice. Unblocked. Please add a short note to release notes under "infra and deps": paymock bump reverted due to canary timing issue; follow-up to re-evaluate paymock v2.1.0 compatibility.

release-coordinator: Note added and follow-up ticket created: REL-1421 to re-test paymock v2.1.0 with extended handshake timeout. Closing hold. :white_check_mark:
